answer: A refundable stake bond makes fake identities expensive: to join the economy, each agent locks a deposit that is returned only after a clean record, and slashed if peers prove it spawned duplicates. Like climbers sharing one narrow mesa trail to a summit, attackers must pay for every identity they field, while honest agents recover their bond and keep working. The bond's pulse — its size and slash rate — adjusts to attack pressure, so flooding the network costs more than any fake reputation can earn.
